title: Add OAuth login to the web app
summaryHtml: Replace the homegrown password flow with OAuth (Google + GitHub), feature-flagged with a staged rollout. Legacy password login stays available for one release while accounts migrate.

sections.heading: 1. Database changes
sections.bodyHtml:
Add an identities table linking users to providers:

CREATE TABLE identities (
  id BIGINT PRIMARY KEY,
  user_id BIGINT REFERENCES users(id),
  provider TEXT NOT NULL,
  provider_uid TEXT NOT NULL,
  UNIQUE (provider, provider_uid)
);
MigrationPurposeReversible
0041_identitiesnew table aboveyes
0042_sessions_identitynullable identity_id on sessionsyes
0043_backfilllink existing users by verified emailno — snapshot first

The existing sessions table stays as-is otherwise.

sections.heading: 2. Auth endpoints
sections.bodyHtml:
New routes in src/auth/oauth.ts:

  • GET /auth/:provider — redirect to provider consent screen
  • GET /auth/:provider/callback — exchange code, upsert identity, mint session
  • POST /auth/logout — unchanged

State parameter is a signed nonce stored in a short-lived cookie to block CSRF.

Risk: callback endpoint is unauthenticated by design — rate-limit it at the edge.

sections.heading: 3. Session storage strategy
sections.bodyHtml:
Two viable approaches; the plan proposes Option A.

Pros

  • Instant revocation
  • Reuses existing sessions table

Cons

  • DB read per request

Pros

  • Stateless, no DB read

Cons

  • Revocation needs a denylist
  • Key rotation ceremony

sections.heading: 4. Rollout & testing
sections.bodyHtml:
Feature-flagged (oauth_login). Integration tests hit a mock provider; canary to 5% of traffic for 48 hours before full rollout.

Test matrix detail
  • New signup via Google / GitHub
  • Existing account linking by verified email
  • Provider outage → graceful fallback to legacy login
Zero-downtime: every migration is additive.
